title: Run the simulation off the render frame and keep the main thread to 2 ms
read_first: PRF-12 frame report and godot/system_overlay.gd,TST-18 frame-time gate (merged partial),PRF-17 worker pool,AUD-12 (audio decode on a worker),Godot _process versus _physics_process and its thread-safety rules for the scene tree,Skyrim.ini Papyrus fUpdateBudgetMS (1.2 ms by default) and the vanilla AI process levels,docs/performance.md,docs/godot-host.md
done_check: User requirement, 2026-10-06: the engine's total budget per rendered frame is 2 ms of main-thread time, and background work does not have to run at the render rate (like asset loading off the UI thread in web pages). On the user's plains walk the engine took about 75 ms of main-thread time a frame plus 121 ms of host frame work, all inline (PRF-34 to PRF-36 have the split). Today PlayerNode::physics_process calls advance on every Godot physics tick (60 Hz, project.godot sets no other rate) and advance runs every game system, AI, magic, detection, Papyrus, quests, inside that tick. When a frame takes longer than one tick, Godot runs up to max_physics_steps_per_frame (8 by default) ticks to catch up, so a slow frame runs the whole game several times and gets slower, a spiral the plains walk shows. Restructure the frame: (1) the render frame on the main thread only applies a ready snapshot of the world (transforms, poses, light and sky state, audio requests) to the Godot scene and draws; (2) the game world (AI, Papyrus, quests, combat, magic, detection, physics bookkeeping) advances on its own thread at a fixed tick (physics 60 Hz, AI and scripts at a configurable lower rate, Papyrus with a per-tick budget like vanilla's fUpdateBudgetMS), and publishes snapshots double buffered so neither side waits; (3) loading, decoding and path searches run on the worker pool and post results; (4) far actors update at lower process levels the way vanilla does. Rendering interpolates between the last two simulation snapshots so movement stays smooth at any frame rate. Godot scene objects are only touched on the main thread. Add a total line to the PRF-12 report and overlay for main-thread engine time per frame, simulation tick time and worker time listed separately, and record the split of the 2 ms in docs/performance.md. The TST-18 gate fails a PRF-12 walkthrough run on installed data in the Bannered Mare or on the Whiterun plains when main-thread engine time exceeds 2 ms at p50 or 4 ms at p99, or when the simulation tick falls behind its rate for more than one second. The physics tick keeps only the player's movement, character controller and Jolt body sync.
